report.verdict: The Star's Q1 FY27 (Sep-26 quarter) is the first positive EBITDA print in more than two years — A$12m (~$8m) vs –A$13m pcp — driven entirely by the two owned properties (Sydney + Gold Coast EBITDA A$35m / ~$24.5m, +164% YoY) and a 29% cut in unallocated corporate costs, partly offset by the Brisbane operator-fee reset (–67%). The operating turnaround is real but small: a ~A$48m annualised group EBITDA run-rate sits below our ~A$70m estimate of annual cash interest (currently paid from a restricted reserve), statutory operating cash flow was still –A$15.5m, cash fell A$28m to A$239m, and the day after the AGM the Federal Court imposed a A$260m (~$182m) AUSTRAC penalty that triggers a WhiteHawk review event. The equity remains a levered option on licence restoration and Bally's continued support, not a cash-flow story yet.

summary: **First positive quarter in >2 years.** Group EBITDA (before significant items, share-based expense and discontinued ops) was A$12m (~$8m) vs a –A$13m loss in Q1 FY26 and –A$9m in Q4 FY26 — a A$25m YoY and A$21m QoQ swing. There is no meaningful sell-side consensus and the company gives no numerical guidance; the market read it as a clear beat against trajectory (shares +13% to A$0.130).

**Revenue A$284m (~$199m), +2% YoY / +8% QoQ — but flat on the originally reported basis.** The pcp was restated down from A$284m (as reported at the Nov-25 AGM) to A$280m with Treasury Brisbane reclassified to discontinued operations. Underlying growth sits in the owned properties (+5% YoY to A$279m), offset by the Brisbane operator fee falling 67% to A$4.5m.

**The owned properties did all the work.** Sydney + Gold Coast segment EBITDA rose to A$35m (~$24.5m) from A$14m pcp (+164%) and A$16m in Q4 (+125%); combined margin 12.5% vs 5.3% pcp (+720bps) and 6.2% in Q4. Sydney A$15m (vs A$3m), Gold Coast A$20m (vs A$11m). Both properties are now EBITDA/operating-cash positive per the Chairman.

**Growth is EGM-led and promo-funded.** Management attributes the revenue recovery at both properties to electronic gaming machine growth 'driven by recent revenue and marketing initiatives'; Sydney table games and cash non-gaming were soft, the latter 'due to increased complimentary investment' and the Sep-25 sale of the Event Centre. No volume/actives/win-rate KPIs are disclosed, so the quality of the EGM growth (visitation vs reinvestment) cannot be verified.

**Cost-out is tangible but has no quantified target or end-date.** Unallocated corporate costs A$23m (~$16m), –A$10m/–29% YoY; group opex A$202m, –12% YoY, falling to 71.1% of revenue from 81.8% (–1,070bps). At FY26 the company said corporate costs fell A$75m in the year and June-quarter annualised corporate costs of A$178m were 38% below FY25. Decentralisation of customer-facing functions to the properties was completed in October; management expects further unallocated-cost reductions, explicitly to 'fund increased marketing investments'.

**Accounting change reduces comparability.** From FY27 corporate shared-service costs are directly attributed to properties (previously a fixed-percentage allocation); FY26 comparatives have been restated with no impact on group EBITDA. Property margins are therefore not comparable with any pre-FY27 disclosure (e.g. Gold Coast H1 FY26 EBITDA of A$15.2m under the old method vs A$11m restated for Q1 FY26 alone).

**Brisbane: record operating result, near-zero economics to Star.** The managed Star Brisbane delivered EBITDAM of A$37m (~$26m), nearly 3x pcp (A$13m) and +43% QoQ, on revenue of A$136m (+14%) — a 27.2% margin; the Chairman says EBITDAM now annualises at >A$150m vs ~A$50m when Bally's took control. But under the CMA amended on 1 Apr 2026 (Stage 1 of the JVP transaction), Star's operator fee was A$4.5m vs A$13.8m pcp and segment EBITDA was nil (vs A$6m). Stage 2 of the transaction is expected by 31 Mar 2027.

**Cash fell A$28m to A$239m (~$167m) in the quarter — and to ~A$200m by the AGM.** Total cash and deposits were A$319m (~$223m) vs A$368m at 30 June, including A$80m of restricted deposits (down from A$101m), of which A$48m is the Interest Reserve Account funding WhiteHawk interest to May 2027. The Chairman told the AGM on 27 Oct the cash balance was 'approximately A$200 million', implying a further ~A$40m outflow in October that the company did not explain (timing of duty/other payments — [unverified]).

**Statutory operating cash flow was –A$15.5m; the 'positive op FCF ex one-offs' claim rests on an unquantified duty payment.** Appendix 4C shows +A$41.5m of one-off receipts (ATO settlement on GST/withholding tax on junket payments, plus returned rebate duty) and an undisclosed one-off payment of historical underpaid NSW casino duty inside operating costs. For management's statement to hold, the duty payment must have exceeded ~A$57m (our arithmetic: 15.5 + 41.5), or ~A$63m after A$5.7m capex. The amount is not disclosed — [unverified].

**Interest is not yet running through operating cash flow.** No interest was paid via the 4C in the quarter; WhiteHawk interest is being met from the Interest Reserve Account through May 2027. With A$48m left to cover ~8 months, implied cash interest is ~A$6m/month (~A$70m+ p.a., ~13% on A$559m) — our estimate, not company-disclosed. From June 2027 this becomes a direct cash drag that exceeds the current ~A$48m annualised group EBITDA run-rate.

**Debt: US$390m (A$559.1m / ~$391m) WhiteHawk senior secured facility, fully drawn, maturing May 2029; no undrawn committed debt.** Loan facilities drawn A$570.7m including the A$11.6m 9% PIK liability to Bally's/Investment Holdings, which was converted on 29 Oct into 105.9m shares at A$0.1123 (Bally's 62.57m, IH 43.35m) following 99.5%+ AGM approval. Unused facilities are only A$6.0m of bank-guarantee headroom. Our net debt estimate: ~A$331m (~$232m) ex restricted deposits, ~A$252m (~$176m) including them; leverage is n/m on LTM EBITDA of ~A$9m.

**Guidance is qualitative and unchanged in direction.** At FY26 (31 Aug) management said it expected to start building cash in FY27 excluding non-operating items; Q1 reiterates that FY27 'is expected to be the first time The Star will generate net annual operating cash inflows, before one-off items, in more than two years' and that 'momentum has continued in October'. No revenue, EBITDA or capex guidance is provided. Note AUSTRAC instalments are 'non-operating' in this framing.

**Post-quarter AUSTRAC judgment (28 Oct): A$260m (~$182m) penalty, accepted.** A$195m attributed to Sydney conduct and A$65m to Queensland, payable in four instalments over 19 months (avg ~A$65m each). AUSTRAC had sought A$400m; Star had argued anything above A$100m risked liquidation. The company says the quantum is 'materially in line with' the FY26 provision and will not affect going concern, but that it constitutes a review event under the WhiteHawk facility; it is in discussions with the lender and 'confident' the facility remains available.

**Licence overhang extended, not resolved.** The NICC advised the Star Sydney licence suspension remains in effect and the Manager's appointment runs to 30 Jun 2027 (unless ended earlier); Queensland confirmed the Gold Coast suspension deferral and Special Manager to 31 Mar 2027 and extended the Brisbane External Adviser to 31 Mar 2027. CEO Mathieson called the outcome 'disappointing'; >85% of remediation-plan milestones are complete. Decentralisation is described as a critical regulatory milestone.

**Going-concern language retained.** The release repeats that liquidity is 'subject to and dependent on the outcome of a number of material uncertainties' (Note G of the FY26 accounts) and that materiality will be reassessed at the H1 FY27 filing (Feb 2027). The 4C's mechanical '15.9 quarters of funding' figure is meaningless against A$260m of penalties.

**Gaming-tax take rising with mix.** Gaming taxes and levies rose 10% YoY to A$70m on +2% revenue — 24.6% of revenue vs 22.9% pcp (+170bps) — consistent with the shift toward higher-duty EGM revenue (Sydney 29.6% vs 28.0%). This is a structural drag on the flow-through of EGM-led growth.

**Ownership and governance.** Bally's holds ~38% and, with Investment Holdings (Mathieson family), ~61% combined; every AGM resolution passed with >96% support. Chairman Soo Kim's remark that this is 'my first and last Annual General Meeting… if the reporting is to be believed' hints at a possible change in listed status — unconfirmed and not addressed further.

**Management rebuild.** New property CEOs John Koster (Sydney) and Ameet Patel (Gold Coast & Brisbane) with property boards; the Gold Coast Tower 2 is delivered and the Andaz hotel opens in November 2026. Star funded A$5.1m of loans and A$1.0m of PP&E for the Destination Gold Coast Consortium JV in the quarter.

**FY26 backdrop for scale.** FY26 normalised revenue A$1,101m (FY25 A$1,125m), normalised EBITDA –A$16.1m (FY25 –A$76m), statutory net loss A$307.3m (FY25 –A$428m) after A$144m of significant items; H1 FY26 average monthly free-cash burn was ~A$20m. Q1 FY27's A$12m EBITDA therefore represents a ~A$100m+ annualised improvement vs the FY26 average quarter but is still thin against ~A$560m of gross debt.

**Thesis read-through.** The bear case (structural revenue decline, uncontrolled cost base) has been answered for now; the remaining case is a balance-sheet and regulatory one. Over the next 19 months Star must fund ~A$260m of penalties plus (from June 2027) ~A$70m p.a. of cash interest from ~A$200m of cash and an EBITDA base that annualises at ~A$48m — the arithmetic only works with continued EBITDA compounding, Brisbane Stage 2, asset/JV monetisation, or further Bally's support.

segments.name: The Star Sydney
segments.headline: EBITDA A$15m (~$10.5m) on flat revenue — a cost and EGM-mix story, with tables and non-gaming still soft and the licence suspension extended to June 2027.
narrative: They reported Sydney revenue of A$162m (~$113m), up 1% on the pcp and 8% on the June quarter, which management describes as strong year-on-year electronic gaming machine growth partially offset by softness in table games and non-gaming. The non-gaming line carries two specific drags: higher complimentary investment (i.e. more of the customer spend is being given back as comps, which reduces reported cash non-gaming revenue), and the loss of events and catering revenue following the sale of the Event Centre in September 2025. Set against a Chairman who told the AGM that the properties had endured roughly three years of double-digit year-on-year monthly declines, a +1% print is the first evidence of stabilisation at Sydney rather than growth; the +8% QoQ move is more encouraging but Q4 FY26 (A$150m) was a weak base.

Gaming taxes and levies rose 7% to A$48m (~$34m) on that 1% revenue increase, taking the tax take to 29.6% of revenue from 28.0% in the pcp (+160bps), which is what one would expect when the mix shifts toward higher-duty EGM revenue and away from tables and non-gaming. Operating expenses fell 13% YoY and 7% QoQ to A$99m (~$69m), or 61.1% of revenue versus 70.2% a year ago — a 910bps improvement that is the real driver of the result. Segment EBITDA of A$15m (~$10.5m) compares with A$3m in the pcp and a A$1m loss in Q4, for a margin of 9.3% (pcp 1.9%, Q4 –0.7%). Management attributes the A$12m YoY improvement to 'stabilisation of revenues and improving cost efficiencies'; on the numbers, essentially all of it is cost.

Two caveats on comparability. First, from FY27 corporate shared-service costs are directly attributed to the properties rather than allocated on a fixed percentage, and the FY26 figures shown here have been restated on that basis — so neither the A$3m pcp EBITDA nor the 9.3% margin can be compared with anything Sydney disclosed before this release. Second, the quarter does not disclose EGM revenue, table drop, win rates, visitation or active members, so we cannot distinguish genuine volume recovery from promotional reinvestment; the rising comp spend and the explicit statement that cost savings will 'fund increased marketing investments' suggest the latter is a meaningful part of the mix. Cash advertising and marketing for the whole group was only A$10.4m (3.6% of revenue) in the quarter, but complimentaries are netted in revenue rather than shown as marketing.

On regulation, the NICC has advised that the Sydney casino licence remains suspended and that the Manager's appointment has been extended to 30 June 2027 unless terminated earlier — a further extension after the September 2025 extension to March 2026. The CEO called this 'disappointing' while noting that more than 85% of remediation milestones are complete and that the decentralised operating model completed in October is itself a regulatory milestone. Post-quarter, A$195m (~$137m) of the A$260m AUSTRAC penalty was attributed to Sydney conduct. The quarter also included a one-off payment of historical underpaid casino duty agreed with NSW Treasury, which the company did not quantify.

Our read: a 9% EBITDA margin for Sydney's only EGM-licensed casino is still a fraction of what the asset earned historically, and the recovery so far is a cost base reset plus EGM promotion, not a table-games or premium-mass rebuild. The path from here depends on whether the Sydney leadership under new property CEO John Koster can hold the opex line while reinvestment rates normalise, and on the NICC decision timeline, which now runs to mid-2027. With roughly A$160m of quarterly revenue, every 100bps of margin is ~A$6.5m of annual EBITDA, so the leverage to even modest table/non-gaming stabilisation is significant — but so is the exposure to the phased NSW gaming-duty increases and to any pull-back in promotional spend.

segments.name: The Star Gold Coast
segments.headline: The cleanest growth story in the group: revenue +12% YoY to A$117m (~$82m), EBITDA +92% to A$20m (~$14m), margin 17.1% — bought with higher marketing, with Andaz opening in November.
narrative: They lifted Gold Coast revenue 12% YoY and 9% QoQ to A$117m (~$82m), with both revenue and EBITDA 'increasing substantially on the pcp due to strong growth in electronic gaming machines, driven by increased marketing investment and promotional initiatives'. This is the second consecutive quarter of sequential growth (Q4 FY26 A$107m) and takes the property back above its Q1 FY26 level with room to spare. As with Sydney, there is no disclosure of EGM turnover, table drop, hotel occupancy or active members, so the growth cannot be decomposed between visitation and reinvestment.

Gaming taxes rose 17% to A$22m (~$15m) — 18.8% of revenue versus 18.1% pcp — again consistent with EGM mix. Operating expenses were A$75m (~$52m), 1% lower YoY but 8% higher QoQ, and management is explicit that the QoQ step-up is marketing. Segment EBITDA of A$20m (~$14m) was up A$9m (+92%) YoY and A$3m (+18%) QoQ, for a 17.1% margin against 10.5% in the pcp (+660bps) and 15.9% in Q4 (+120bps). The flow-through tells the story: YoY, A$12m of incremental revenue produced A$9m of incremental EBITDA (~75%, flattered by the restated cost allocation and cost-out), whereas QoQ, A$10m of extra revenue produced only A$3m of EBITDA (~30%) because A$6m of it went straight back into marketing. That is the marginal cost of the growth they are buying.

The property is also the group's main capital call. Star funded A$5.1m of loans to the Destination Gold Coast Consortium joint venture and A$1.0m of PP&E on its behalf in the quarter (shown as related-party investing payments), and received A$0.4m of dividends. The Chairman confirmed Tower 2 has been delivered and the Andaz hotel opens in November 2026, adding room inventory into the seasonally strongest December quarter. The Stage 1 DBC unwind transferred the JV partners' Gold Coast interests to Star in exchange for its share of Brisbane and the Treasury property, so the Gold Coast is where any asset-value optionality now sits.

Regulatory oversight persists: Queensland has confirmed the deferral of the Gold Coast licence suspension and extended the Special Manager's appointment to 31 March 2027 (previously 30 September 2026), and A$65m (~$46m) of the AUSTRAC penalty was attributed to Queensland conduct. Operationally, Ameet Patel has taken over as property CEO for both Gold Coast and Brisbane.

Our read: the Gold Coast is the one property where the growth is unambiguous and the margin is already respectable for a regional integrated resort, and the Andaz opening gives a clear near-term catalyst. The risk is the opposite of Sydney's — that opex (marketing) is scaling with revenue, so the incremental margin from here is closer to 30% than 75%. We would want to see the QoQ opex growth decouple from revenue growth over the next two quarters before extrapolating the 17% margin higher.

segments.name: The Star Brisbane (managed) & Treasury Brisbane (discontinued)
segments.headline: Record EBITDAM of A$37m (~$26m) for the managed resort, but Star's operator fee fell 67% to A$4.5m and the segment contributed nil EBITDA — a capability showcase with no P&L.
narrative: They recognise only the operator fee from The Star Brisbane as revenue, and that fee was A$4.5m (~$3m) in the quarter against A$13.8m in the pcp (–67%) and flat on Q4 FY26. The reset follows the amended Casino Management Agreement with Destination Brisbane Consortium that took effect on 1 April 2026 on completion of Stage 1 of the JVP transaction, under which Star transferred its share of Star Brisbane and the Treasury property, was released from a A$700m debt guarantee and received the JV partners' Gold Coast interests. Directly attributable overheads of A$5m (–37% YoY) absorbed the entire fee, leaving segment EBITDA at nil versus A$6m in the pcp — a A$6m YoY drag that offsets a fifth of the owned-property improvement at group level.

The managed property itself had its best quarter on record. Revenue was A$136m (~$95m), up 14% YoY and 12% QoQ, and EBITDAM — EBITDA before Star's management fee charged to DBC — was A$37m (~$26m), nearly triple the A$13m pcp and 43% above Q4's A$26m, for a 27.2% margin (pcp 10.9%, Q4 21.5%). Chairman Kim told the AGM that EBITDAM 'now annualises to more than A$150 million as compared to just A$50 million annualised when we took over'. Management is careful to define EBITDAM as the performance of operations under Star's remit, excluding costs DBC incurs directly as owner, and says it should be read as an operating-trend indicator rather than a consolidated metric.

That framing matters for valuation. Star Brisbane's A$148m annualised EBITDAM run-rate is nearly three times the whole listed group's A$48m annualised EBITDA, yet none of it accrues to SGR shareholders beyond the ~A$18m p.a. fee stream, which currently runs at roughly break-even after attributable costs. The release does not disclose whether the amended CMA includes any incentive or performance component, so we treat fee upside as [unverified]. Stage 2 of the JVP transaction remains subject to conditions and was expected by 31 March 2027 at the FY26 results; the Brisbane External Adviser's appointment has also been extended to 31 March 2027. Treasury Brisbane stays in discontinued operations with nil EBITDA in the quarter.

Our read: Brisbane is the clearest proof that the Bally's/Mathieson operating playbook works in the Australian regulatory environment — a 27% EBITDAM margin on a new-build IR with an External Adviser in place is a strong result — and it strengthens the group's case for suitability with the Queensland regulator. For the equity, however, it is an advertisement rather than earnings: Star's economic exposure here is now a low-margin management contract plus whatever is embedded in Stage 2. Management chose to lead the release with the EBITDAM record; the operator fee line is where the group's actual earnings sit, and it is the only line that went backwards.

segments.name: Corporate, cash flow & balance sheet
segments.headline: Unallocated corporate costs –29% to A$23m, but statutory operating cash flow was –A$15.5m, cash fell A$28m to A$239m (and ~A$200m by the AGM), interest is being paid from a reserve that runs out in May 2027, and A$260m of AUSTRAC penalties now sit on top.
narrative: They reported unallocated corporate costs of A$23m (~$16m), down A$10m or 29% YoY and 4% QoQ, equal to 8.1% of group revenue versus 11.8% in the pcp. Under the new direct-attribution methodology, this residual covers remediation, legal and compliance oversight, technology, audit, tax and consolidated reporting; customer-facing functions were pushed to the properties during the quarter and the Chairman said decentralisation of operational control was completed in October. Management expects unallocated costs to fall further as the model embeds and says cost-out at both properties and corporate is ongoing 'in order to fund increased marketing investments'. For scale, at FY26 the group said corporate costs fell A$75m in the year and June-quarter annualised corporate costs (pre-attribution) of A$178m were 38% below FY25 — but no quantified FY27 target or end-state has been given.

The Appendix 4C shows the cash reality beneath the A$12m EBITDA. Receipts from customers were A$334.4m (~$234m; above revenue because of GST and DBC labour recharged at cost), against A$178.1m of operating cost payments, A$177.5m of staff costs (53% of receipts), A$25.8m of administration and corporate costs, A$10.4m of advertising and marketing (3.6% of revenue) and A$2.0m of lease payments. Interest received was A$2.5m and 'other' receipts of A$41.5m comprised the one-off ATO settlement on GST/withholding tax on junket payments plus returned rebate duty on previously written-off debts. Net operating cash flow was –A$15.5m (~–$11m); investing was –A$10.4m (capex A$5.7m, DGCC JV loans A$5.1m, dividends +A$0.4m); financing was –A$0.1m; and a –A$1.7m FX effect took cash and equivalents from A$267.1m to A$239.4m.

Management's statement that 'operating free cash flow excluding one-off items was positive' therefore hinges on the size of the one-off payment of historical underpaid NSW casino duty buried in operating costs, which is not disclosed. Stripping out the A$41.5m of one-off receipts leaves underlying operating cash flow of –A$57.0m before that payment, so the duty payment must have exceeded ~A$57m (or ~A$63m after capex) for the claim to hold — plausible given prior-year provisioning but [unverified]. Separately, no interest was paid through operating cash flow: the WhiteHawk coupon is being drawn from the A$48m Interest Reserve Account, which funds payments to May 2027. Restricted deposits fell A$21m to A$80m in the quarter, consistent with an interest draw plus reduced bank-guarantee collateral (our inference). With A$48m covering roughly eight more months, implied cash interest is ~A$6m per month, or ~A$70m+ per year — roughly 13% on the A$559m facility — which is our estimate, not a company figure. The Chairman also told the AGM that cash was 'approximately A$200 million', some A$40m below the 30 September balance, without explanation.

On the liability side, the US$390m WhiteHawk senior secured facility (A$559.1m / ~$391m at 30 September) is fully drawn and matures in May 2029; total loan facilities drawn were A$570.7m including the A$11.6m PIK liability to Bally's and Investment Holdings accruing at 9%, which was converted on 29 October into 105,917,185 shares at A$0.1123 following AGM approval (99.5–99.7% in favour). Unused facilities are just A$6.0m of headroom under a A$15.3m Westpac bank-guarantee line — there is no undrawn revolver. On our estimate net debt is ~A$331m (~$232m) excluding restricted deposits or ~A$252m (~$176m) including them, and leverage is not meaningful on LTM EBITDA of ~A$9m. One day after the quarterly, the Federal Court imposed the A$260m (~$182m) AUSTRAC penalty — materially in line with the FY26 provision, payable in four instalments over 19 months — which the company says triggers a review event under the WhiteHawk facility; it is in discussions with the lender and 'confident' the facility will remain available. The going-concern material-uncertainty language from Note G of the FY26 accounts is repeated and will be reassessed at the half-year.

Our read: the cost programme is delivering and the properties are now self-funding at the EBITDA line, but the group is not. Over the next 19 months Star faces ~A$260m of penalty instalments (~A$65m average), the exhaustion of the interest reserve in May 2027 followed by ~A$70m p.a. of cash interest, DGCC funding calls and maintenance capex, against ~A$200m of unrestricted cash, ~A$30m of restricted non-IRA deposits and an EBITDA base running at ~A$48m annualised. Management's 'net operating cash inflows before one-off items' framing is achievable on our numbers; 'building cash reserves' in any meaningful sense is not unless EBITDA compounds quickly, Stage 2 of the Brisbane transaction releases value, or Bally's provides further support. The WhiteHawk review-event outcome is the single most important near-term disclosure.

highlights.text: Owned-property EBITDA (Sydney + Gold Coast) rose A$21m YoY to A$35m (~$24.5m) with margin +720bps to 12.5%; both properties are now EBITDA-positive and the group printed its first positive EBITDA (A$12m / ~$8m) in more than two years.

Cost base reset is visible in the numbers: group opex –12% YoY to A$202m (71.1% of revenue, –1,070bps), unallocated corporate –29% to A$23m, decentralisation completed in October with further reductions flagged.

First YoY revenue growth at the owned properties (+5% to A$279m) since quarterly reporting began in Q1 FY25, following ~3 years of double-digit monthly declines; management says momentum continued in October and the Gold Coast Andaz opens in November.

Star Brisbane EBITDAM hit a record A$37m (~$26m), nearly 3x pcp, at a 27.2% margin and annualising >A$150m — strong evidence of operating capability and a supportive data point for Queensland suitability.

AUSTRAC penalty landed at A$260m (~$182m) — well below the A$400m sought, in line with the FY26 provision, and payable over 19 months — removing the largest binary liability from the going-concern equation (post-quarter, 28 Oct).

Management reiterated that FY27 should be the first year of net operating cash inflows before one-off items in more than two years, with Q1 operating free cash flow excluding one-offs stated as positive.

lowlights.text: Brisbane operator fee –67% to A$4.5m under the amended CMA; the segment now contributes nil EBITDA (vs A$6m pcp) and group revenue was flat on the originally reported Q1 FY26 base (A$284m).

Statutory operating cash flow was –A$15.5m and cash fell A$28m to A$239m (~A$200m by the AGM per the Chairman); the 'positive op FCF ex one-offs' claim depends on an unquantified NSW duty payment that our arithmetic says must have exceeded ~A$57m.
Interest is being paid from a A$48m reserve that runs out in May 2027; implied cash interest of ~A$70m p.a. (our estimate) exceeds the current ~A$48m annualised group EBITDA run-rate.

Sydney licence suspension continues with the Manager extended to 30 Jun 2027; Gold Coast Special Manager and Brisbane External Adviser extended to 31 Mar 2027 — management itself called the outcome 'disappointing'.

The A$260m AUSTRAC penalty constitutes a review event under the fully drawn WhiteHawk facility (no undrawn revolver; A$6m unused facilities) and going-concern material-uncertainty language is repeated pending the H1 FY27 assessment.

Growth quality is unproven: EGM-led and funded by higher complimentaries and marketing (Gold Coast opex +8% QoQ, ~30% incremental flow-through), Sydney tables and non-gaming still soft, and gaming-tax take up 170bps of revenue on mix.

Disclosure is thin and comparability is impaired: no P&L below EBITDA, no actives/visitation/win-rate KPIs, FY26 property comparatives restated under a new cost-attribution method, and the one-off cash items are not quantified.

forecast.intro: Star does not issue numerical guidance; its outlook statements are qualitative. At the FY26 result (31 Aug 2026) management said it expected to start building cash in FY27 excluding non-operating items, with July owned-property revenue +6% YoY. The Q1 FY27 release holds that line — 'FY27 is expected to be the first time The Star will generate net annual operating cash inflows, before one-off items, in more than two years' — and adds that momentum continued into October. The A$25m YoY EBITDA improvement was driven by the owned properties (+A$21m: Sydney +A$12m, Gold Coast +A$9m) and the corporate cost programme (+A$10m), partly offset by the Brisbane operator-fee reset (–A$6m). The A$260m AUSTRAC penalty, confirmed the day after the release, is treated by management as non-operating and is not captured in that framing.

bridge.title: Group EBITDA Q1 FY26 → Q1 FY27

forecast.view: **Q2 FY27 (Dec-26 quarter, our estimate): group EBITDA A$15–25m (~$10–18m)** on owned-property revenue of ~A$290–305m (+6–10% YoY), helped by holiday-season seasonality, the Andaz opening and continued EGM momentum, with corporate costs ~A$21–22m and the Brisbane fee ~A$4.5m. **FY27 (est.): revenue A$1.10–1.13bn (~$0.77–0.79bn), roughly flat on FY26's A$1,101m** because the ~A$42m lower operator fee absorbs most of the owned-property growth; **group EBITDA A$55–85m (~$39–60m), a 5–7% margin, vs –A$16m in FY26**, predicated on owned-property EBITDA holding at A$35–45m per quarter and unallocated corporate drifting toward A$20m. **Leverage direction: net debt rises.** Gross debt is USD-denominated (A$559m at 0.6975) and stable to maturity in May 2029, but unrestricted cash of ~A$200m must absorb ~A$260m of AUSTRAC instalments over 19 months, DGCC funding, maintenance capex and — from June 2027 — ~A$70m p.a. of cash interest (our estimate). On our FY27 EBITDA range net debt/EBITDA stays >5x and is unlikely to be a meaningful metric before FY28; the equity case remains dependent on EBITDA compounding toward A$100m+, Brisbane Stage 2, and continued Bally's support. **Swing factors:** the WhiteHawk review-event outcome (terms, fees, any covenant reset); the timing and size of the first AUSTRAC instalment; NICC/Queensland licence decisions (Mar/Jun 2027); promotional reinvestment discipline at the Gold Coast; Sydney table-games stabilisation; and the phased NSW gaming-duty step-ups.
watch: WhiteHawk review-event resolution — any amended pricing, fees, covenants or additional security, and whether the ~A$50m additional liquidity provision referenced at signing remains available.
First AUSTRAC instalment (amount and date) and the cash balance at 31 Dec 2026 in the Q2 FY27 4C; reconciliation of the ~A$40m Oct-26 cash drop flagged by the Chairman.
H1 FY27 results (Feb 2027): going-concern assessment, quantification of the one-off NSW duty payment and ATO receipts, P&L below EBITDA including interest expense, and any impairment.
Regulatory calendar: Gold Coast Special Manager and Brisbane External Adviser to 31 Mar 2027; Sydney Manager to 30 Jun 2027; any NICC commentary on a path to licence reinstatement.
Brisbane JVP Stage 2 completion by 31 Mar 2027 and disclosure of the amended CMA fee economics (base vs incentive).
Monthly owned-property revenue trajectory through the Dec-26 quarter (Andaz opening, holiday season) and whether Gold Coast opex growth decouples from revenue growth.
Interest Reserve Account run-off toward May 2027 and the transition of ~A$70m p.a. (est.) of cash interest into operating cash flow.
